correctness.rationale: For the DCT-renormed spaces, standard basis vectors give C_q^r(U_n)>=n^(1/q)/2. A contraction interpolation lemma combines Wu's q=2 Gaussian-cotype bound with a Gaussian one-coordinate lower bound to give C_q^g(U_n)<=C(n/log(n+1))^(1/q). The flat orthogonal matrix calculation gives ||U_n||_{q,1}<=2^(1/(2q)) n^(1/(2q)) (2 log(2n))^(1/(2q)), which is below the same target scale for all q>=2 once n is universally large. The DCT rows are orthonormal and uniformly O(n^(-1/2)), so the Hadamard-order restriction is unnecessary.

originality.rationale: The current arXiv:2609.19731v1 states the negative result only for q=2 and n=2^k. Searches by identifier, title, operator-cotype terminology, q>2, and (q,1)-summing terminology found no public extension to every finite q. Talagrand's monograph gives a positive theorem for full l_infinity domains, and Junge's C(K) comparison results do not cover these subspace-domain counterexamples. Classical interpolation and orthogonal-transform ingredients are excluded from the novelty claim.

value.rationale: The result expands a new endpoint counterexample into a simultaneous family covering every finite cotype exponent and identifies a sharp qualitative inheritance boundary: Talagrand's positive full-l_infinity-domain estimate is not uniformly inherited by explicit graph subspaces. The all-dimension DCT realization also removes an arithmetic restriction of the original construction.
